headers.//: Astro fingerprints these filenames, so a changed file is a changed URL. They can be cached forever.
Video and poster are not fingerprinted — cached for a month, so replacing them still lands within a sensible window.
Social preview and icon: long enough to be free, short enough to fix a mistake.

HTML always revalidates, so a deploy is visible on the next request rather than an hour later. Both patterns are needed: Firebase matches headers on the REQUEST path, and with cleanUrls the home page is requested as `/`, which never matches `**/*.html`. Firebase's default of max-age=3600 applies otherwise, and this page carries a version number and download links that change every release.
Same reason as `/` above, for the other locale: cleanUrls means this is requested as `/es`, which matches neither `/` nor `**/*.html`.
Baseline hardening for a static marketing site. No frames, no MIME sniffing, no referrer leakage to third parties.
